findings.where: Article page specimen, the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The quote is static text set in logo blue. The palette gives that blue to links and the button, so the reserved link colour is borrowed for emphasis. On a reading page where the related link right below it is the same blue, a reader can mistake the quote for a link and tap it, and nothing happens.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader on an article page who taps the blue line expecting it to open the cited law or a source, and gets no response. Angélique also loses a clear rule that blue means a link when she adds posts.

findings.where: Hero, the primary “Get in touch →” button (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one action is a bare mailto link. The arrow suggests it goes to a page, but it hands off to whatever mail app the device has, and the address isn't shown anywhere on the page. On a work machine with webmail only, or no mail client set up, the click does nothing visible or opens an unwanted app, and the visitor can't copy an address instead.
findings.who_objects: Staff at multilateral banks on locked-down corporate laptops who use webmail. The action the site exists for fails for them with no fallback.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the “Play again” button below the timeline table
findings.fault: The button seems to replay the hero heading's entrance, since the table names “Heading, line 1/line 2” and the sketch has no demo heading of its own. That heading is a full screen or more above the button. Pressing it replays the motion out of view, so nothing seems to happen and the control looks dead.
findings.who_objects: Mark or the founder reviewing the tile. They press Play again to judge the motion, see no change, and can't assess the one motion principle the tile exists to show.

findings.fault: The button is styled exactly like the article's link, as underlined blue text. The underline is reserved for links, so one look stands for two functions on the same tile: going somewhere and doing something here.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds that take their signifiers from this tile. If they copy it, buttons and links will look the same across the site.
